\chapter{Programming Guide}
\label{ch:programming-guide}

\guidechapterintro{This chapter organises the same language by function. It explains the structure of a Croqtile program, its type system, symbolic shapes, parallelism, tile selection, data movement, contraction and coordination, and the reasoning behind them. Complete kernels sit beside the feature they demonstrate, so each section also stands on its own.}

\section{Program Structure and Compilation Models}
\label{sec:3-1}

\guideslotintro{A \file{.co} program is transpiled into host and device code. The three layers that result decide which parts the compiler rewrites and which it passes through, and the same split supports both single-source and separate-source compilation.}

\section{Symbolic Shapes, Shape Evaluation, and Value Numbering}

\guideslotintro{A dimension does not have to be a literal. \texttt{mdspan} accepts anonymous dimensions filled in by the caller and symbolic dimensions evaluated by the compiler; value numbering is what lets the compiler fold the resulting expressions and still prove shapes safe.}
